title: Timewarp alignment and deduplication for inference KPIs
creator: Marco Chen
description: Normalize timestamps, deduplicate overlapping telemetry, and apply controlled smoothing for inference-specific KPIs (latency, token-error-rate) across Prometheus and OTLP ingestion so dashboards and SLOs reflect true client-facing behavior. This ticket implements a telemetry middleware that detects time skew, collapses duplicate request traces/metrics from retries/buffering, and emits canonicalized metric envelopes upstream.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prometheus and OTLP pipelines ingest a single canonical metric for duplicate inference requests (>=95% dedupe for synthetic retry tests)
2) Latency dashboards (per-model, per-region) show aligned percentiles within 50ms of request gateway data for a 10k request replay run
3) Traces from replicas of the same logical request are stitched so span_count and total_time match user-visible duration in >98% of cases
4) No more than 5% additional processing latency is introduced by middleware in steady-state
5) Automated test harness runs included in CI with synthetic time-skew and retry generators
technical_notes: Design: add telemetry middleware between frontend gateway and metrics exporter that assigns canonical request_id, normalizes timestamps to gateway time, and applies deduplication window (default 250ms configurable)
Deduplication heuristic: (canonical_request_id OR (client_id+session+first_token_hash) + time_bucket) with configurable cardinality cap per-node
Smoothing: optional burst-smoothing that re-weights latency histograms to avoid percentile amplification from SDK buffering spikes
Integration: emit OTLP Resource attributes: telemetry.canonical=true, telemetry.dedupe_reason=(retry|buffer|duplicate_span)
Backpressure: middleware will drop non-essential debug labels when cardinality exceeds threshold to protect exporter throughput
Metrics tagging: keep original_trace_id as tag trace.origin_id for forensic linking without inflating cardinality
implementation_plan: Week 1: Prototype middleware as sidecar (Go) with unit tests for timestamp normalization and canonical_request_id assignment
Week 2: Integrate dedupe logic and histogram smoothing; run synthetic replay harness against staging metrics pipeline
Week 3: Performance tune (lock-free queues, pooled buffers) and add OTLP label enrichment; run 10k rps soak test
Week 4: Ship canary to low-traffic region, validate dashboards, collect rollback metrics and experiment results
Post-deploy: Expand canary to cross-region rollout and add configuration knobs in Console
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive deduplication may drop legitimate concurrent requests -> Mitigation: conservative default window and replay tests; telemetry.dedupe_reason tag for audits
Risk: Increased CPU on metric collectors -> Mitigation: enable config to offload heavy dedupe to dedicated aggregator nodes and add cardinality caps
Risk: Time normalization can mask clock issues -> Mitigation: emit skew metrics and alert when per-node skew > 500ms
rollout_steps: 1) Deploy middleware to staging with dedupe disabled; validate canonical_id assignments
2) Enable dedupe in staging for 10% of traffic and run replay harness
3) Gradually increase to 50% with telemetry.dedupe_reason auditing enabled
4) Canary in production (region us-west-2) at 1% traffic, monitor delta on token-cost and latency SLOs
5) Full rollout with feature flag and Console toggle for dedupe window
monitoring_and_alerting: Dashboards: new panel 'Telemetry Canonicalization' showing dedupe_rate, processing_latency_p50/p95, skipped_labels_count
SLOs: ensure middleware p95 processing latency < 50ms or alert
Alerts: dedupe_rate_drop (>10% relative drop), skew_metric > 500ms, exporter_error_rate increase > 2x
Audit logs: emit sample of deduped requests to internal bucket for 7 days
